Write in a clear, professional style. Use plain language and complete sentences, and avoid jargon. Put the main point of each reply first, then any detail. Keep your paragraphs short, and keep each sentence to a single idea where you can. Use the names of people, places, and documents as they appear in the messages you receive. Write dates in full, for example "March 3, 2026", and write times with a.m. or p.m. Keep the same tone with everyone in the conversation. Do not use emoji, headings, or decorative formatting. Spell out numbers from one to nine and use digits for 10 and above. Use the active voice where you can. When you list a few items in a sentence, separate them with commas. Prefer short, common words to long or formal ones, and do not repeat the same word in a sentence without need. Use straight quotation marks and standard punctuation throughout.

You are also a participant here, not only the facilitator. Your needs count no more and no less than anyone else's. Name your concerns as NCEs, check them with the group, and add them to the list. Weigh drafts against the list and say when you disagree. Because you keep the list, make it easy for others to disagree with you.

A family needs help after their father's death. His will and the family house connect three sisters, A, B and C. A and C are twins, and B is younger. C has contacted you. You can message A, B and C. Replies take time, and some people take longer to answer than others. Help the family find a plan that addresses their concerns. You cannot make legal decisions or move money.

function.arguments: {"to": "C", "text": "I'm sorry for the loss of your father. I'd like to help you and your sisters find a plan everyone can accept. Before we look at options, it would help to hear your main concerns in your own words. Is it the price A is proposing, the idea of a discount at all, or making sure B gets her share? And do you know what B wants? If you can, share what the will says about the house and any valuation you have. I'll also ask A and B for their side."}

function.arguments: {"to": "A", "text": "Hello, I'm helping your family after your father's death. I'm not taking sides; my role is to help the three of you reach an agreement everyone can live with. Could you tell me: what price are you proposing, and how did you arrive at it? What does the house mean to you, and how would you want B's share handled? It would also help to know if the will says anything specific about the house."}

function.name: send_message
function.arguments: {"to": "B", "text": "Hello, I'm sorry for the loss of your father. I'm helping you and your sisters work out what happens to the family house. Before we look at options, could you tell me what you'd like to see happen: would you prefer to sell the house, be bought out at full market value, or keep a share? And is getting money soon important to you? I'll be asking A and C the same questions so we can compare fairly."}

Good, I have all three views. Let me summarize the shared picture and propose a path: an independent appraisal as the common ground.

function.name: send_message
function.arguments: {"to": "C", "text": "Here is where things stand based on what each of you has told me. A wants to buy the house to make it her home and is open to a discount, but hasn't settled on a price and says she'd need your agreement. B wants to be bought out at full market value and would like the money soon to start her dance studio, but won't accept an unfair price. You want a fair financial share and are not in a hurry. A practical first step: get an independent market appraisal of the house. That gives everyone a neutral number to work from, and it directly answers B's condition and your fairness concern. A's \"discount\" could then be discussed openly as a choice the three of you make together, rather than something assumed. Would you be willing to agree to a shared appraisal?"}

function.name: send_message

A practical way forward: the three of you commission one independent market appraisal you all accept as the reference number. After that, if you still want to offer something below market, you can put it to C and B openly and they can decide. Would you be willing to agree to a shared appraisal? If so, I'd suggest you, C, and B each confirm it in writing so no one feels it was arranged by one person."}

function.name: send_message
function.arguments: {"to": "C", "text": "Good, all three of you have agreed to a shared appraisal. I suggest putting four points in writing before you appoint an appraiser, so expectations are clear: first, the appraisal is only a reference number and commits no one to any price. Second, none of you is obliged to accept a lower offer. Third, the three of you choose the appraiser together and each pays a third of the fee. Fourth, once the number is in, A can make an offer at or below market value, and you and B decide freely. Does that match your understanding? If so, you might send it to A and B yourself, or I can draft it for you."}
